items.prompt: Which word is formed by blending the sounds /p/ /ĭ/ /g/?
items.rationale: Pushing the three sounds /p/, /ĭ/, and /g/ together forms the word “pig.”

items.prompt: In which order should a learner blend the sounds in the word “top”?
items.rationale: The word “top” begins with /t/, has /ŏ/ in the middle, and ends with /p/.

items.prompt: Which action shows a learner correctly blending /h/ /ă/ /t/?
choices: Pushes the sounds together and says “hat”
Says each sound as a separate word
items.answer: Pushes the sounds together and says “hat”
items.rationale: Blending means pushing the individual sounds together to read the whole word “hat.”

items.prompt: What happens when the sounds /p/ /ĭ/ /g/ are blended?
choices: They stay as three separate words.
items.rationale: Blending joins the individual sounds in order so the learner can read the whole word “pig.”

items.prompt: Which word is made by blending the letter sounds /k/ /ă/ /t/?
items.rationale: Blending /k/ /ă/ /t/ gives c-a-t, so “cat” is the correct word.

items.prompt: Which word has the short i sound?
items.rationale: The i in “sit” makes the short /ĭ/ sound; the other choices have short a.

items.prompt: Which word starts with /m/ and ends with /p/?
items.rationale: “Map” starts with /m/ and ends with /p/, with short a in the middle.

items.prompt: Which word uses the short a sound in the middle?
items.rationale: The middle vowel in “bat” is short a; the middle vowels in the other choices are short i.

items.prompt: Which word has a short u sound?
items.rationale: Cut is sounded out as /k/ /u/ /t/, with a short u sound.

items.prompt: Which word is made by blending the sounds /m/, /o/, and /p/?
items.rationale: Blending /m/, /o/, and /p/ makes the word mop.

items.prompt: In which word does the middle letter make a short e sound?
items.rationale: Hen is sounded out as /h/ /e/ /n/, with a short e sound.

items.prompt: A word starts with /m/ and ends with /p/. Which spelling has a short o sound in the middle?
items.rationale: Mop is sounded out as /m/ /o/ /p/, with a short o sound.

items.prompt: Which word ends with “-ng”?
items.rationale: “Ring” ends with “-ng,” which makes one sound.

items.prompt: Which word ends with “-nk”?
items.rationale: “Bank” ends with the joined letters “-nk,” which make one sound.

items.prompt: Which word is formed by adding “-ng” to “ri”?
items.rationale: Adding “-ng” to “ri” forms “ring.”

items.prompt: Which choice is the sight word that starts with s and ends with d?
items.rationale: “Said” is a Set 4 sight word, and it starts with s and ends with d.

items.prompt: Which choice is the three-letter sight word that starts with w?
items.rationale: “Was” is a Set 4 sight word with three letters, and it starts with w.

items.prompt: Which choice is the sight word with the letter r in the middle?
items.rationale: “Are” is a Set 4 sight word, and r is its middle letter.

items.prompt: Which choice is the sight word that starts with th and ends with y?
items.rationale: “They” is a Set 4 sight word, and it starts with th and ends with y.

items.prompt: The sentence reads, “The cat is asleep.” Which voice should you use when reading it?
items.rationale: A period shows that a statement is complete. A calm, flat voice fits this sentence.

items.prompt: Which punctuation mark should end the sentence: “Do you like apples”
items.rationale: The sentence asks a question, so it needs a question mark to show a rising, questioning voice.

items.prompt: The sentence reads, “Can you help me?” Which voice should you use when reading it?
items.rationale: A question mark signals that the sentence is asking something, so the voice should rise with curiosity.

items.prompt: Which punctuation mark should end an announcement that should be read with excitement: “The show has started”
items.rationale: An exclamation mark shows strong excitement and helps the announcement sound lively and enthusiastic.

items.prompt: Choose the sight word that asks for the name of something.
items.rationale: “What” is the sight word used to ask for the name or identity of something.

items.prompt: Choose the sight word that asks about a place.
items.rationale: “Where” is the sight word used to ask about a place or location.

items.prompt: Choose the sight word that means to direct your eyes toward something.
items.rationale: “Look” is the sight word used to direct one’s eyes toward something.

items.prompt: Choose the sight word used when inviting someone to move closer.
items.rationale: “Come” is the sight word used to invite someone to move closer.

items.prompt: Which word begins with two consonant sounds?
items.rationale: The word “frog” begins with the consonant blend “fr,” so its first two letters make two consonant sounds.

items.prompt: Which word ends with two consonant sounds?
items.rationale: The word “lamp” ends with the consonant blend “mp,” so its last two letters make two consonant sounds.

items.prompt: Which letters make the blend at the beginning of “stop”?
items.rationale: The beginning of “stop” has the consonant blend “st.”

items.prompt: Which letters make the blend at the end of “lamp”?
items.rationale: The ending of “lamp” has the consonant blend “mp.”

items.prompt: A story line says, “The cat sat on the mat.” How should you read it aloud?
choices: Read every word by itself, with a short pause after each word.
Read the words in order with a smooth, natural phrase.
Read only the story’s character and action words.
Read the words from right to left, one word at a time.
items.answer: Read the words in order with a smooth, natural phrase.
items.rationale: Reading the words in order with a smooth, natural phrase shows accurate, fluent reading.

items.prompt: A story line says, “The sun is up. The dog wakes.” How should you read it aloud?
choices: Read the first sentence, pause, then read the second sentence.
Pause after every word in both sentences.
Read the second sentence first, then read the first sentence.
Read both sentences in one long, unbreakable phrase.
items.answer: Read the first sentence, pause, then read the second sentence.
items.rationale: A brief pause at the end of the first sentence helps the reader continue smoothly and accurately.

items.prompt: While reading aloud, you say “mop” instead of “map.” What is the best way to keep your reading accurate?
choices: Keep going and hope the mistake does not change the story.
Go back, say “map,” and then continue reading the sentence.
Change the story so that “mop” makes sense.
Skip the rest of the sentence and begin the next one.
items.answer: Go back, say “map,” and then continue reading the sentence.
items.rationale: Going back, correcting the word, and continuing keeps the reading accurate without stopping the story for long.

items.prompt: A story line says, “I can hop,” said Nan. How should you read this line aloud?
choices: Read the dialogue in a natural voice, pause, then read “said Nan.”
Read the dialogue in a whisper, pause, then read “said Nan.”
Read “said Nan” first, pause, then read the dialogue.
Read the whole line in one voice without a small pause.
items.answer: Read the dialogue in a natural voice, pause, then read “said Nan.”
items.rationale: Reading the dialogue naturally and pausing before the speaker’s words gives the line accurate, smooth phrasing.

items.prompt: Which word starts with the sh sound?
items.rationale: In “ship,” the letters s and h work together to make the /sh/ sound.

items.prompt: Which word ends with the th sound?
items.rationale: In “bath,” the letters t and h work together to make one /th/ sound at the end of the word.

items.prompt: Which word begins with the wh sound?
items.rationale: In “whale,” the letters w and h work together to make the /w/ sound at the beginning of the word.

items.prompt: Mia had a red block. Her brother Jon gave it to her. Who gave Mia the block?
items.rationale: The text says that Jon gave Mia the block.

items.prompt: Nora looked for her shoes. She found them under her bed. Where were the shoes?
items.rationale: The text says that Nora found her shoes under her bed.

items.prompt: Ana baked cookies for lunch. She placed them on a plate. Who baked the cookies?
items.rationale: The text says that Ana baked the cookies.

items.prompt: Jamal is playing basketball with his friends. When the ball rolls away, Jamal runs after it and gets it back. Who is the story about?
items.rationale: Jamal is the main character because the story focuses on his actions during the game.

items.prompt: Anna visits a place where a librarian helps her find a book. She and Dad sit quietly and read together. Where does the story take place?
items.rationale: The librarian, books, and quiet reading show that Anna and Dad are in the library.

items.prompt: Nia put on her shoes and took a ball. At the park, she played on the swings. Which choice tells who the story is about and where it takes place?
items.rationale: Nia is the main character, and the story takes place at the park.

items.prompt: Read one sentence: “Milo put the cup on the table for the cat.” Who put the cup on the table?
items.rationale: Milo is the subject of the sentence and is the one putting the cup on the table.

items.prompt: Ana put a bean in the soil. A plant grew, and a yellow flower opened. Which event belongs at the beginning?
items.rationale: Planting the bean happens first, before the plant grows and the flower opens.

items.prompt: Bo woke up, ate breakfast, brushed his teeth, put on his coat, and left for school. When did Bo brush his teeth?
choices: After Bo put on his coat.
items.rationale: Brushing his teeth comes after breakfast but before putting on his coat, so it is in the middle.

items.prompt: Kim saw a dark cloud, rain began, and then sunshine spread across the sky. Which event belongs at the end of the story?
items.rationale: The sun appearing comes after the cloud arrives and the rain begins, so it is the ending.

items.prompt: Which word is read with a long a sound?
items.rationale: The silent e makes the a in cake say its long sound, /ā/.

items.prompt: Which word has a long i sound?
items.rationale: The silent e makes the i in bike say its long sound, /ī/.

items.prompt: Which word ends with a silent e and has a long o sound?
items.rationale: The final e in note is silent, and the o is read with its long sound, /ō/.

items.prompt: Which sentence contains a word that does not make sense?
choices: The cat ran across the floor and drank a book.
The dog ran across the floor and drank milk.
The bird flew over the tree and ate worms.
The girl jumped over the chair and drank water.
items.answer: The cat ran across the floor and drank a book.
items.rationale: A cat cannot drink a book, so this sentence contains a word that does not make sense.

items.prompt: Which sentence fixes the mistake in “The fish climbed a tree and ate a worm”?
choices: The fish swam in a pond and ate a worm.
The fish climbed a pond and ate a worm.
The fish swam in a tree and ate a worm.
The fish flew in a pond and ate a worm.
items.answer: The fish swam in a pond and ate a worm.
items.rationale: A fish can swim in a pond, so this sentence fixes the words that did not make sense.

items.prompt: I notice that “The bird used a shovel to eat a worm” does not make sense. What should I do next?
choices: Reread it and replace the word.
Skip it and turn to another page.
Change bird to dog and keep going.
Read it again without changing it.
items.answer: Reread it and replace the word.
items.rationale: Rereading the sentence and replacing the wrong word with one that fits fixes the mistake.

items.prompt: Which word completes the sentence: “I ___ to play outside.”
items.rationale: “I want to play outside” is complete because “want” expresses what the speaker wishes to do.

items.prompt: Which word means “a number of things, but not all”?
items.rationale: “Some” means an amount of things that is not the whole amount.

items.prompt: Which word is used to report someone’s words?
items.rationale: “Said” is used to show that someone spoke, as in “Ana said hello.”

items.prompt: Which word means “at or in that place,” not “in this place”?
items.rationale: “There” means at or in that place, while “here” means in this place.

items.prompt: Which word has a long a sound?
items.rationale: In “made,” the a says its long sound, /ā/, as in the word “day.”

items.prompt: Which word has a short u sound?
items.rationale: In “jump,” the u says its short sound, /ŭ/, rather than its long sound, /ū/.

items.prompt: In the word “kit,” which type of vowel sound does the i make?
items.rationale: The i in “kit” says its short sound, /ĭ/, so it is a short vowel sound.

items.prompt: Which word has a long o sound?
items.rationale: In “note,” the o says its long sound, /ō/, while the o in the other words is short.

items.prompt: Mia ___ the puppy every day.
items.rationale: “Feeds” means gives food regularly. The -s ending helps show that Mia does this action.

items.prompt: There are three ___ on the table.
items.rationale: “Dishes” means more than one dish. The -es ending is added to dish when the word ends in sh.

items.prompt: Yesterday, we ___ to the park.
items.rationale: “Walked” describes an action that happened in the past. The -ed ending shows that the walking was yesterday.

items.prompt: Who is speaking in the sentence “I climbed the big tree”?
items.rationale: The word “I” refers to the character who climbed the tree and is speaking.

items.prompt: Which sentence has a character telling the story?
choices: The girl found a shiny leaf.
items.rationale: The pronoun “I” shows that a character inside the story is telling it.

items.prompt: In “Mia lost her ball. She looked for it,” who is telling the story?
items.rationale: The narrator describes Mia in the third person, so someone outside the story is telling it.

items.prompt: In “I helped my mother,” what does the word “I” show?
choices: It shows the speaker's point of view.
It gives the speaker's full name.
It shows an outside narrator's viewpoint.
items.answer: It shows the speaker's point of view.
items.rationale: The word “I” identifies the character who is speaking and shows that the story is told from that character's point of view.

items.prompt: Which word can be split into two smaller words that both make sense?
items.rationale: “Sunset” splits into “sun” and “set,” which are both smaller words.

items.prompt: A child wants to read a word naming a small cake served in a cup. Which split works?
items.rationale: The two smaller words are “cup” and “cake.” Together, they make “cupcake.”

items.prompt: Which split shows the two words in “bookcase”?
items.rationale: “Bookcase” splits into the smaller words “book” and “case.”

items.prompt: What does the contraction “can’t” stand for?
items.rationale: “Can’t” combines “can” and “not,” so it means “can not.”

items.prompt: Which contraction belongs in the sentence: “_____ raining outside today”?
items.rationale: “It’s” stands for “it is,” so the sentence means that it is raining outside today.

items.prompt: In the sentence “I’m ready to read,” which two words does the contraction mean?
items.rationale: “I’m” combines “I” and “am,” so it means “I am.”

items.prompt: Nia jumped out of her seat and shouted, “Yes! Let’s play right now!” What feeling does Nia most likely have?
items.rationale: Nia’s jump, shout, and eager words show that she feels excited.

items.prompt: After the test, Kim pointed to the paper and said, “I got every one right!” Kim most likely feels
items.rationale: Kim’s words show that he feels proud of getting every answer right.

items.prompt: When her cousin arrived, Tara ran to him, hugged him, and said, “I missed you!” Tara most likely feels
items.rationale: Tara’s hug and words show that she feels happy to see her cousin again.

items.prompt: A ball rolled toward Jo. Jo stepped back, held his hands close to his chest, and said, “Please don’t throw it!” Jo most likely feels
items.rationale: Jo’s steps backward, tight hands, and request show that he feels scared.

items.prompt: Which word has the long a sound?
items.rationale: In “rain,” the vowel team ai makes the a sound long.

items.prompt: Which word uses ee to spell the long e sound?
items.rationale: In “feet,” the vowel team ee makes the e sound long.

items.prompt: Which word has the long o sound?
items.rationale: In “boat,” the vowel team oa represents the long o sound, as in “coat.”

items.prompt: Which word rhymes with “feet”?
items.rationale: “Beat” and “feet” have the same long e sound and rhyme. The ea in “beat” represents the long e sound.

items.prompt: Which word is made from the sounds /f/, /l/, and long /ī/?
items.rationale: The sounds /f-l-ī/ spell “fly,” where y sounds like long i.

items.prompt: Which word rhymes with funny?
items.rationale: Sunny and funny both have the long e sound at the end, so they rhyme.

items.prompt: Which phrase from a poem helps you hear a sound?
items.rationale: “Rang loudly” describes a sound, so this phrase helps the reader hear the bell.

items.prompt: Which phrase from a story helps you see what something looks like?
items.rationale: A rainbow can be seen, so this phrase helps the reader picture the sky.

items.prompt: Which phrase from a story helps you feel how something feels when touched?
items.rationale: “Fur felt soft” tells how the puppy’s fur feels when it is touched.

items.prompt: Which phrase from a poem helps you taste something?
items.rationale: “Tasted salty” describes how the soup tastes to the person eating it.

items.prompt: How many vowel sounds are in the word picnic?
items.rationale: Picnic is read pic-nic, with one vowel sound in each part, for two vowel sounds total.

items.prompt: Which word has two vowel sounds?
items.rationale: Candle is read can-dle, with two vowel sounds: a and e.

items.prompt: Which vowel sound comes first in the word rabbit?
items.rationale: Rabbit is read rab-bit, so its first vowel sound is short a.

items.prompt: Which word is made of three vowel-sound parts?
items.rationale: Sunflower is read sun-flow-er, with one vowel sound in each of its three parts.
